newsitem.title: USA: British nanny may soon face murder charge.
newsitem.headline: British nanny may soon face murder charge.

text.p: An 18-year-old British nanny, accused of battering a 9-month-old infant in her charge, may face a murder charge if the child dies, a prosecutor told reporters on Friday after a court hearing.

Prosecutor Lynn Rooney had told a Massachusetts county court that parents Sunil and Deborah Eatten were meeting Friday to decide if their baby boy, Matthew, should be kept on life support, without which he will likely die.
"If the baby should not survive, the Commonwealth will seek a murder indictment," Rooney told reporters after the hearing.

The nanny, Louise Woodward, 18, was arrested Wednesday on charges of assault and battery on a child under the age of 14. The baby remained in critical condition at Boston's Children's Hospital, a spokeswoman said.

At the Middlesex County Court hearing, Woodward was seeking to have her $100,000 bail reduced. Her attorney, Maria Galvagna, told the court, "This woman poses absolutely no danger to the community or to any other person for that matter."
Rooney said the cause of the infant's injuries "was a violent shaking in combination with blunt force trauma. The doctors have made it absolutely clear that it was an inflicted injury."

The prosecutor told reporters earlier this week that under questioning, Woodward, who first told police that she was just trying to revive the infant who had been feeling sickly all day, admitted she had shaken the child. The child was rushed to the hospital Tuesday afternoon.

"At that time, she gave a statement indicating that she had, in fact, shaken the baby earlier in the afternoon because the baby had been fussy and had been crying violently and she was frustrated," Rooney said.
Woodward, who arrived in the United States in June from Chester, England, has been living with and working for the child's parents since November, according to court records.
The baby's parents, Sunil and Deborah Eatten, are both doctors, authorities said.
